newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - DLR VOLS SOFT AS SPOT SAGS, STG VOLS BID.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - DLR VOLS SOFT AS SPOT SAGS, STG VOLS BID.

text.p: Implied volatilities for most dollar-pair options were soft in U.S. trading as the greenback drifted well below Wednesday's highs, traders said.
Sterling volatilities, however, remained well bid as the pound extended recent losses after the Bank of England's quarter-point rate rise.

"Everything got hit this morning, although it's stabilized right now," said an interbank broker in New York, referring to dollar/mark and dollar/yen volatilities. He added that there was still good interest in the upside strike prices, which probably meant the dollar's slide was seen to be short-lived.
The dollar, which had peaked on Wednesday just below the key 1.90-mark and 120-yen levels, was hovering around 1.87 marks and the mid-118 yen area at U.S. midsession.

Dollar/mark implied volatility curve had become very flat, with one-month out to one-year all trading at around 11.2/11.4 percent, little changed from late Wednesday in the front months and a touch softer in the back end.
The front end was underpinned by a purchase of $1 billion in notional value of one-week mark calls with a strike price of 1.85 marks, said MaryBeth Slack, FX options analyst at MCM OptionWatch.
She added that the dollar/yen curve had also begun flattening late on Wednesday after several million dollars worth of one-year option selling.

"There had been a lot of buying in the back end late last week and early this week, but it looks like it's over with," she said. "Money center banks are out of there, so these vol levels should come off."
One-year dollar/yen fell to 11.9/12.1 percent from Wednesday's highs near 13 percent. One-month had fallen to 11.1/11.3 percent from Wednesday's 11.9/12.1 close and 12.4/12.6 highs.
Sterling/dollar and sterling/mark volatilities were firm as the pound continued shedding the sharp gains from the May-July rally fuelled by anticipation of tighter credit.

"The reason behind that (today's slide in spot) clearly is that although they got the interest rate hike, comments out of MPC (BOE's monetary policy committee) suggested that there won't be any more hikes in the near term," Slack said.
With the sterlings' appreciation this year seen casting shadows over the health of British exporters, traders saw further retracement lower in the pound.

One-month cable was nearly half a point higher on the day at 10.2/10.5 percent as spot tumbled below $1.58 before clawing slightly back up. Sterling had been as high as mid-$1.62s on Wednesday and just short of $1.70 in mid-July.
One-month stering/mark jumped more than a full point to 12.0/12.3 percent as spot fell below 3.00 marks.
